name: Master of Information Technology
description: This two-year course takes graduates from other fields and builds working knowledge of programming, databases, networks and systems analysis. Students learn through weekly labs and team projects that run from a client brief to a delivered system. A supervised placement is offered in the second year.

name: Master of Health Informatics
description: Students learn how clinical information is recorded, coded, moved between services and turned into reports. Teaching mixes lectures on health data standards with practical work on patient record systems and privacy rules. The course suits people from clinical, administrative or computing backgrounds.

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: A one-year entry course covering the practical basics of computing. Students build simple websites, set up small networks and learn how to look after common business software. Most of the work is hands-on, in the lab.

name: Master of Software Engineering
description: Covers the whole life of a software product, from gathering requirements through design, testing and maintenance. Students work in teams on a long project using the same review and release habits found in working software groups. Later units look at architecture, quality assurance and the safe handling of faults.

name: Master of Network Engineering
description: Focuses on how data networks are planned, built and kept running. Students configure routers, switches and wireless equipment in a lab, then move on to larger designs that cover traffic control and fault recovery. A final project asks for a full network design with a written justification.

name: Diploma of Game Design
description: An introduction to how games are planned and made. Students sketch levels, write simple scripts in a game engine and test their work with other students. The course ends with a small playable game made in a group.

name: Master of Interaction Design and Usability
description: A one-year course in designing digital products around the way people think and act. Students interview users, draw prototypes, run usability sessions and revise their work from the results. The studio units are taught in small groups with regular critique.

name: Master of Information Systems
description: Looks at how organisations choose, build and run the information systems they depend on. Teaching is by case study and workshop, with students analysing real processes and proposing system changes. Technical units on data and security sit beside units on governance and change.

name: Master of Information Technology Management
description: Prepares graduates to lead technology work in an organisation. Students study project planning, service management, budgeting for systems and the basics of security. Assessment uses reports, group projects and a placement or industry-set research task.

name: Master of Software Development
description: A programming-heavy course for graduates who want to write software for a living. Students learn several languages, build web and mobile applications and practise writing clear, tested code. Group units simulate a development team with regular releases.

name: Master of Telecommunications and Networks
description: Teaches how voice, video and data travel across wired and wireless links. Early units cover signals and protocols; later units cover network planning and the management of large systems. Lab work uses real equipment as well as simulators.

name: Master of Game Development
description: Students make games from the ground up, writing the code, shaping the rules and building the tools the game needs. Much of the course runs as studio projects where small teams ship a playable build each semester. Theory units cover graphics, physics and the structure of game engines.

name: Diploma of Applied Information Technology
description: A practical one-year diploma that gives a broad start in computing. Students learn to build and fix computers, write short programs and manage files and users on a small network. It is designed to lead into a degree or into support work.

name: Master of Digital Health
description: A one-year course on how digital tools are changing the delivery of health care. Students look at electronic records, remote care, data sharing and the risks that come with them. Teaching is through case studies and a project set by a health service.

name: Master of User Experience Design
description: Teaches how to research, design and test the screens people use every day. Students move between workshops and long design projects, building a portfolio of case studies. Units cover accessibility, interface patterns and how to present design choices to a client.

name: Diploma of Web Development
description: Students learn to build websites from scratch using markup, styling and scripting. Weekly practical tasks add up to a small site that works on phones and laptops. The last unit covers putting a site online and keeping it running.

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: A two-year practical course that moves from computer basics into networks, programming and systems support. Classes are mostly workshops with real equipment, and a work placement is part of the second year. Graduates can go on to further study or to support and administration work.

name: Diploma of Network Administration
description: Teaches how to set up and look after a small to medium business network. Students install servers, manage user accounts, configure wireless and fix common faults. Almost every unit is taught in a lab.

name: Diploma of Software Development
description: This two-year course teaches students to write programs in more than one language and to build working applications. They learn version control, testing and basic design, and finish with a team project. Time on placement gives a taste of working in a development group.

name: Diploma of Web Development and Design
description: A hands-on diploma for people who want to make and maintain websites. Students write markup and scripts, lay out pages for different screens and connect pages to a simple database. They also learn how to plan a site with a client.

name: Diploma of Game Development
description: Students are taught to build small games using a common game engine. They write scripts, create simple models and sound, and put a level together for others to play. Group work through the second year follows a real production schedule.

name: Diploma of Health Information Systems
description: A one-year diploma for people who want to work with patient and service records. Students learn how records are kept, coded and protected, and practise with sample record software. Units also cover the privacy rules that apply to health data.

name: Diploma of User Interface Design
description: Introduces the design of screens for websites and apps. Students sketch layouts, build clickable prototypes and test them with classmates. Colour, type and plain-language writing are covered along the way.

name: Diploma of IT Support and Systems Administration
description: Prepares students for the daily work of keeping a business running on its computers. They learn to troubleshoot desktops, manage accounts, back up data and write clear help guides for users. A placement in a support team forms part of the second year.

name: Master of Information Technology
description: A conversion course for graduates new to computing. Students begin with programming and data, then choose units in web, mobile or systems work. The course leans on projects with outside organisations, and a placement is available in the final year.

name: Master of Information Systems Management
description: Looks at how information systems support the work of an organisation and how to manage them well. Students analyse processes, plan system changes and consider risk and cost. Assessment is mostly case studies and group reports.

name: Master of Applied Software Development
description: Teaches practical software work through repeated build-and-review cycles. Students write code in teams, review each other's work and learn to handle changing requirements. The course covers design, testing and the tools used to release software.

name: Master of Network and Systems Administration
description: A one-year course for graduates who want to run networks and servers. Students build and manage systems in a lab, from address planning to server roles and monitoring. Units on security and automation use scripting throughout.

name: Master of Health Informatics
description: Students learn how health information is collected, shared and used to improve care. The course blends lectures with practical work using sample clinical systems and data sets. A placement or industry project in the second year ties the learning to a real service.
units: Ethics and Privacy in Health Data

name: Master of Human-Computer Interaction
description: Examines how people use technology and how products can be shaped to suit them. Students plan studies, interpret what users say and do, and build prototypes to test ideas. A research project in the second year asks for an original study.

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: A short foundation course in computing, aimed at people with little prior experience. Students write their first programs, learn how computers store information and try basic network tasks. It is a path into a university degree.

name: Master of Interactive Media and Game Design
description: Combines game design with wider interactive media such as installations and educational tools. Students write code, shape player experience and test their work in front of audiences. Most units are studios where students show progress to staff and peers every week.

name: Master of Information Technology
description: A broad course that gives graduates from any background a working grounding in computing. Students learn programming, data handling and systems design, then choose a specialist strand. Studio-style subjects use projects set by outside organisations, with placements available.

name: Master of Information Systems Practice
description: Combines technical and organisational study of information systems. Students learn to analyse a business problem, design a system response and manage its delivery. Subjects are taught as workshops where students work through case material in teams.

name: Master of Software Engineering Practice
description: Students practise engineering software in teams, from early requirements to final release. The course covers architecture, testing, security and the habits of long-lived codebases. Studio subjects are assessed on the quality of both the product and the working process.

name: Master of Networked Systems
description: Covers the design and operation of connected systems, from local networks to large distributed services. Students build and measure networks in the lab and study how to make them fast and reliable. Later subjects turn to automation, monitoring and security.

name: Master of Health Technology and Informatics
description: Explores how technology is used in health settings, from record systems to monitoring devices. Students analyse health data, learn the rules that protect it and work on projects with health partners. The course draws on both computing and health science staff.

name: Master of Interaction Design and Digital Experience
description: A one-year studio course on designing digital products, services and spaces. Students research users, prototype quickly and criticise one another's work in regular reviews. By the end they have a portfolio of finished projects.

name: Master of Game Design and Production
description: Students learn to design, prototype and produce games as part of a small studio. The course covers game rules, level construction, scheduling and how to run playtests. Each semester ends with a build presented to a panel of staff.

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: A one-year diploma that prepares students for degree-level computing study. They work on programming, how computers and networks are put together, and the writing and teamwork needed later on. Classes are small and mostly practical.

name: Master of Information Technology
description: A two-year course for graduates in any discipline who want a technical career. The first year teaches programming, data and systems; the second allows a specialisation and a larger project. Students may take a placement in a technology team.

name: Master of Information Technology Management
description: Teaches the management side of technology. Students study how to plan projects, manage technical staff, purchase systems and protect information. Teaching is a blend of lectures, group case work and a final management project.

name: Master of Software Engineering Studies
description: Teaches software design, construction and testing with an emphasis on large systems. Students work on long projects in which requirements change and code must be kept in good shape. Later units look at cloud services and the safe use of data.

name: Master of Network Security and Infrastructure
description: Looks at building networks that can stand up to attack. Students design and configure secure infrastructure, study how attacks work and practise detecting and responding to them. Most weeks include a lab exercise on live systems.

name: Master of Health Data and Informatics
description: Students work with the data that health services collect and learn to make it useful and safe. Units cover record systems, data quality, statistics for health and the ethics of data use. A project in the second year is carried out with a health partner.

name: Master of Human-Centred Design
description: Trains students to design technology around real needs. They spend much of their time in the field and the studio, interviewing people, shaping ideas and testing them with users. Subjects look at accessibility, ethics and communicating design decisions.

name: Master of Games Technology
description: A technical course on the software behind games. Students write graphics code, build physics and artificial intelligence systems and work with a game engine at a low level. A group project at the end produces a complete game.

name: Diploma of Information Technology Foundations
description: A one-year pathway course covering the core ideas of computing. Students program in small steps, learn how data is stored and meet the basics of networks. Lectures are supported by regular small-group tutorials.

name: Master of Information Technology
description: A flexible two-year conversion course for graduates new to the field. Students study programming, data and systems, then choose a focus for the second year. The course has a strong project flavour, with team work for outside clients and a placement option.

name: Master of Software Development
description: Students become confident programmers and designers of software systems. Weekly studios have them build applications in teams, with reviews and testing built into every cycle. They also meet cloud services and secure coding in the second year.

name: Master of Network Engineering
description: This course covers the principles and practice of building data networks. Students configure and measure networks, study the protocols that run them and design larger systems for given needs. A final project asks for a design that is built and tested in the lab.

name: Master of Game Design
description: Focuses on the craft of designing games that people want to keep playing. Students analyse existing games, write design documents and build prototypes that are playtested in class. Production units teach planning and teamwork in a studio setting.

name: Master of Health Informatics Practice
description: A one-year course on putting health information to work. Students study clinical record systems, the standards that let them share data and the rules for handling personal information. Practical units use realistic data sets, and a placement is offered.

name: Master of User Experience Practice
description: A one-year practical course in designing digital experiences. Students carry out user research, build prototypes and test them, then refine their work from what they learn. Most subjects are taught in studios with frequent feedback.

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: A one-year diploma that introduces programming, databases and websites. Students learn by building small projects and working through lab exercises each week. It prepares them for study in a degree.

name: Diploma of Interactive Games Programming
description: A two-year diploma for students who want to program games. They learn a mainstream language, work with a game engine and add graphics, sound and simple artificial intelligence. Each year ends with a game made by a small team.

name: Master of Information Technology
description: A general technology course for graduates from other areas. Students begin with programming and data, then move to systems, networks and a specialist strand. Group projects use real briefs, and a work placement is available.

name: Master of Information Systems
description: Teaches how information systems are planned, built and governed in an organisation. Students look at process analysis, enterprise software, data and security. Teaching includes workshops, case studies and a capstone problem for a partner organisation.

name: Master of Software Engineering
description: Students learn to build dependable software at scale. The course covers requirements, design, testing, security and delivery pipelines, with long group projects at its centre. A work placement gives practice in a team environment.

name: Master of Computer Networking
description: A one-year course that teaches how to design, build and manage computer networks. Students practise in a lab with routers, switches and servers, and learn to diagnose faults under time pressure. Units on virtual and cloud networks finish the program.

name: Master of Digital Health Systems
description: Examines the technology behind modern health services, including records, messaging between providers and remote care tools. Students learn to assess systems, work with health data and consider patient privacy. Projects are often done with regional health providers.

name: Master of Interaction and Experience Design
description: Teaches the design of interactive products through research, prototyping and evaluation. Students work on projects across screens, devices and physical spaces. Studio subjects emphasise clear communication of design reasoning.

name: Master of Game Technology
description: A two-year course that mixes game programming, graphics and design. Students build small games in the first year and a larger team project in the second. Technical units explain how engines manage rendering, input and simulation.

name: Diploma of Information Technology Support
description: A practical one-year diploma in the everyday work of supporting computer users. Students learn to set up and repair machines, look after accounts and resolve user problems politely and clearly. It also covers basic networks and security habits.

name: Master of Information Technology
description: A conversion course for graduates who wish to enter computing. Students study programming, databases, web systems and project work, then choose electives in the second year. Smaller class sizes allow close contact with staff, and a placement is available.

name: Master of Business Information Systems
description: Links business needs with technology choices. Students analyse how organisations work, learn to specify and select systems and study the management of data. Case studies and a final project with a local organisation form most of the assessment.

name: Master of Software Development
description: Students gain strong programming skills and learn how to build, test and release applications. The course alternates between workshops on a new technique and projects where it is applied. In the second year students lead a team on a larger piece of software.

name: Master of Networks and Cloud Infrastructure
description: Teaches how modern networks and cloud platforms are designed and run. Students configure real and virtual systems, automate routine tasks and study how to keep services available. A project in the second year tests a design under simulated load.

name: Master of Health Informatics
description: A one-year course on how health data is created, stored and used. Students examine record systems, standards for sharing information and methods for analysing health data. The program draws on local health services for projects and placements.

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: A one-year entry diploma into computing. Students write simple programs, create websites and learn how computers are connected. Small classes give plenty of time with tutors.

name: Master of Digital Interaction Design
description: A compact course about designing digital tools that suit their users. Students plan research with real people, prototype ideas and test them in repeated rounds. Design briefs often come from community and island businesses.

name: Master of Game Design
description: Students learn game design by making games, starting with paper and small digital prototypes. They write scripts in an engine, balance rules and run playtests with outside players. The final project is a game developed over a full semester in a small team.
